meta.title: Finding Gold — GIS and remote sensing

meta.description: Finding Gold: a field guide to mineral exploration. Educational — not a design standard.

dialogue.speaker: zawadi
dialogue.text: One geologist maps a few square kilometres in a day. A satellite images a hundred thousand.

dialogue.speaker: zawadi
dialogue.text: Remote sensing works because minerals absorb light at particular wavelengths. Rock looks grey to us. To a sensor, it has a fingerprint.

dialogue.speaker: zawadi
dialogue.text: Landsat 8 and 9 give eleven bands at thirty metres, and cost nothing. Sentinel-2 gives thirteen bands at ten metres. And ASTER carries the short-wave infrared that actually identifies alteration minerals.

dialogue.speaker: zawadi
dialogue.text: Hydrothermal fluid does not only deposit gold. It rots the rock around it, for tens or hundreds of metres. That is the alteration halo — and the halo is a far bigger target than the vein.

dialogue.speaker: zawadi
dialogue.text: The halo has a mineralogy you can see from orbit. Clays, sericite, iron oxides, silica. You find them with band ratios: divide one band by another, so the ratio spikes exactly where that mineral absorbs.

dialogue.speaker: zawadi
dialogue.text: Then structure. A digital elevation model gives you topography, and topography remembers geology — because faults erode into valleys, and hard beds stand up as ridges.

dialogue.speaker: zawadi
dialogue.text: Shade the model from several directions, and the lineaments come out.

dialogue.speaker: zawadi
dialogue.text: And intersections matter. Where two structures cross, the rock is more broken, so fluid moved more easily, so gold is likelier. A great many deposits sit on intersections.

dialogue.speaker: zawadi
dialogue.text: Now GIS earns its name. Every dataset is a layer. Geology, alteration, lineaments, stream gold, soil gold, magnetics, old workings. Stack them in register.

dialogue.speaker: zawadi
dialogue.text: Score each layer for how much it predicts, weight it, add them up, and you have a prospectivity map. Not an answer. A ranking.

dialogue.speaker: juma
dialogue.text: So the computer picks the target?

dialogue.speaker: zawadi
dialogue.text: The computer ranks the ground. Then you go and stand on it.

dialogue.speaker: zawadi
dialogue.text: Every anomaly is a hypothesis until somebody ground-truths it. Half of them turn out to be a dirt road, a dry lake bed, or a roof.
